item.description:
New

  • Flows save results to files: the Write File block writes JSON, JSON Lines, CSV, TSV, a workbook, Markdown or an HTML page, can append or keep both when the file exists, and can ask you where to save.
  • Flows get an Ask a Model block, which asks the model from Settings › Assistant once. Blocks can be grouped under a title and coloured.
  • Responses can be checked against the request's GraphQL schema.
  • The MCP Servers page lists resource templates, with a field for each variable. A server's sampling request can be answered by your model, and you read the answer before it goes back.

Improved

  • WebSocket, Socket.IO and GraphQL subscriptions send the request's auth with the upgrade (Hawk, OAuth 1.0, EdgeGrid, AWS, Digest). MQTT publishes carry 5.0 properties.
  • Automatic headers such as User-Agent, Accept and Cookie can be switched off per request. The Settings tab shows only what the request's kind uses. Copy as cURL and Generate Code include Hawk, OAuth 1.0 and EdgeGrid signatures.
  • The Assistant's tool calls live in a tray behind the composer. The conversation keeps only the words.
  • A copy of a workspace asks before it uses the original's secrets and permissions.
  • Quick Send (the menu bar panel) is removed. The Shortcuts actions stay.

Fixed

  • Two security audits: hostile responses, specs and servers can no longer crash or hang Echolot, redirects no longer carry secrets to other hosts, and agents see only what the safety model allows.
  • Fixed edits lost on a reload or quit, slow opening of large JSON and long lines, sheets in Marine, and the onboarding tour.

New

  • Mocks stream: routes play server-sent events, take WebSocket and Socket.IO connections, and a mock can run an MQTT broker beside its port. JavaScript routes take sockets too.
  • gRPC requests can run as live calls: send messages one at a time and see answers as they arrive.
  • Webhooks can be signed: a sender's HMAC signature lets a delivery in without the token, and tokens can be rotated.
  • Agents make every kind of request, set OAuth 2.0 client-credentials auth, and keep WebSocket, Socket.IO and MQTT sessions open across calls (the new Sessions toolset, with Stop in the Agents popover).
  • Agents can propose a script: you see the diff and choose Save and Trust or Decline.
  • Suites check WebSocket, Socket.IO and MQTT sessions: checks and captures on received messages, message counts and closes, and a request can stop listening once it has what it needs.
  • The Tests page runs checks with Run and Run All; the Runner filters its results by Passed and Failed.
  • The command palette (⌘K) finds flows, specs, mocks and MCP servers by name.
  • GraphQL requests can share one query file, and a request can name its own spec for openapi checks.

Improved

  • Released builds no longer ask for Keychain access: the app and the command-line tool share their secrets. Variable editors warn about short secrets and ordinary words.
  • Schedules and webhooks can name their environment and never run in a protected one they didn't name. `echolot mcp serve` moves to the app when the app opens the workspace.
  • `echolot run` keeps captured values in memory unless --save-captures, and never sends a request whose variables don't resolve.

Fixed

  • Fixed gRPC reflection with relative type names, MQTT brokers that only speak 3.1.1, and a few layouts that ran past their pane in French and Russian.

New

  • Settings › About shows when a beta build expires, with the days left.
  • The Assistant's CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) start their current ACP adapters; accounts made from an old preset move to the new command by themselves.

Improved

  • Sending stays fast as history fills up: a send no longer scans the whole history or waits for the disk (a 20,000-entry history fills four times faster).
  • New workspaces come with a .gitattributes, so Git never changes the line endings of their files, and exports keep it.

Fixed

  • A request deleted outside Echolot while you edit it is no longer written back: a bar offers Save Again or Discard.
  • Environment names and secret values are saved when you leave the field, trimmed, and an environment can no longer be left without a name.
  • Global variables changed in one window reach every open window.
  • Stopping a send stops following its response, and reconnecting a WebSocket, Socket.IO or MQTT session never closes the newer connection.
  • New MCP and gRPC calls can be undone, and flow prompts and MCP input requests wait their turn instead of replacing each other.
  • Allow Access grants only the file Echolot asked for.
  • Opening several specs quickly shows the last one opened.

New

  • Echolot now speaks French, German, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Russian and Simplified Chinese. It follows the system language, or pick one in Settings › General › Language.
  • A guided tour on first launch, to replay from Help › Show the Tour.
  • The Assistant panel resizes: drag its edge (double-click restores the default).
  • Mocks answer spec operations that have no example with fresh fake data that fits each field.

Improved

  • Echo, the status screen in the page header, is on by default.
  • In the Assistant's approval sheet, Allow for This Session now covers every change to the workspace at once; deleting still asks.
  • The welcome window gets a sonar ping behind the app icon.

Fixed

  • The request editor no longer draws over the response.
  • Home fits a narrow window, so a wide Assistant no longer pushes it over the sidebar.
  • Echo's greeting is no longer squeezed, and the Assistant's title stays on one line in every language.
  • Removing a test with its minus button no longer crashes Echolot, and neither does removing an MQTT subscription or message, a WebSocket message or a Socket.IO emit. Thanks to Amit for reporting it.
  • The minus button in the Flows list deletes the selected flow; it used to take clicks only on its thin line.

New

  • Home's Sonar card plots every send of the last hour, 24 hours, 7 or 30 days by response time, with sends, answered OK, median and p95 against the period before.
  • Marine, a second dark appearance in deep-water blues (Settings › General › Appearance).
  • Workspace auth from any request: the Auth tab opens the folder or workspace auth a request inherits (Workspace Auth… for one with its own), and folder and workspace settings sign in with OAuth 2.0 once for every request that inherits.
  • More auth: OAuth 1.0, OAuth 2.0's password grant and Advanced settings, and Postman's ASAP auth imported as JWT Bearer.
  • Agents and the Assistant can give requests auth and captures (credentials only as {{variables}}), set a folder's auth, and try a flow once after you approve it; Settings › Assistant › Ask before can limit questions to deleting, new hosts and protected environments.
  • Requests whose last call failed show a warning sign in the requests list, with what went wrong.

Improved

  • The Assistant's replies render as Markdown and stay smooth while they stream.
  • Flow cards show what they do, conditions are edited as rules, and an Evaluate block's last expression is its result.
  • Settings › Storage shows how much room response bodies take, and Remove Stored Bodies… frees it.
  • On smaller screens the Assistant and pinned variables no longer push the window past the screen: the variables float instead.

Fixed

  • Security fixes from two audits: OAuth tokens are kept per environment and settings and never go to another host; agents can't write credentials into files or send secrets to new hosts without asking; stopped mock, MCP and webhook servers close every connection.
  • Fixed a crash on very large numbers in values, HTTPS proxies failing with HTTP/2 servers, text ending in """ changing when saved, and moves or renames wiping open tabs' undo.
  • With encryption at rest on, history no longer keeps request bodies in plain text.
  • Workspace and folder settings follow your appearance, Marine included, and keep one size when you switch tabs.
  • The gRPC call bar fits its pane: long proto, service and method names are cut short instead of running into the response.

New

  • Mocks no longer need a spec: make routes by hand (method, path with {id}, status, headers, body and rules on the request), with fake data in their bodies: {{$randomFullName}}, {{request.params.id}}, {{#repeat 10}}…{{/repeat}}. Create Requests turns a mock's routes into requests.
  • The same fake values work in requests, and echolot fake writes fake data from a template on the command line.
  • Select several requests in the sidebar to put them in a new folder (New Folder with N Items) or change their headers, query parameters and auth at once (Edit N Requests…).
  • Echo, an optional status screen in the page header (Settings › General › Echo), tells what happens in the window, and a click unrolls a report of the session.
  • Help › Echolot Documentation (⌘?) opens the new documentation at docs.echolot.dev, and Help › Help for This Page the page about what you're looking at.

Improved

  • Echolot asks once per model provider before sending anything to it; Settings › Assistant lists what you've allowed, with Revoke. Apple's on-device model and servers on your Mac never ask.
  • After an update nothing opens by itself: a What's New button in the page header shows the new notes.
  • The command palette offers only what makes sense on the page showing.
  • JSON responses show \u escapes as the characters they stand for.
  • The sidebar's highlight glides from row to row, and the module switcher springs to the module you pick.

Fixed

  • Add Rule and Add Header keep the row they add and put the cursor in it.
  • The window's traffic lights no longer sit cut off when another window comes to the front.

Improved

  • Protected environments ask before more things: MCP calls, checks and watches, Get Token, schema fetches, gRPC reflection and messages sent on an open session after you switch environments.
  • A proxy password or certificate passphrase kept as plain text now carries a warning, with Move to Keychain beside it; clearing one request's history asks first.
  • Typing {{ offers the request's variables again in the URL bar, and the variables a folder's or workspace's auth resolves with in their settings.
  • The JSON tree opens large responses sooner, and the flow canvas pans more smoothly.

Fixed

  • Secrets stay put: API key headers and headers holding a secret no longer follow a redirect to another origin, history no longer keeps Hawk, EdgeGrid, NTLM, proxy or certificate secrets, and with encrypted storage a response's text stays out of the search index.
  • Agents read history with credentials masked, and a search match that touches a secret is neither counted nor shown; an agent's limits also hold inside the flows it runs.
  • NTLM sign-in works over HTTP/1.1 without another request borrowing its connection, and a server that insists on HTTP/1.1 gets it. HTTP/3 tries every address of a host at once, as TCP does.
  • Responses that expand absurdly (past 100 to 1 beyond 256 MB), and WebSocket and Socket.IO messages built from huge fragments, are cut off instead of filling memory.
  • Export never writes over, into or around the workspace it comes from, sends what it replaces to the Trash, and says how many credentials were written in clear.
  • Edits are no longer lost: folder and workspace settings, mock routes and a tab closing just before you quit are all written, and a failed save keeps your text.
  • Closing a window stops its runs and sends. Runs with iterations side by side keep their own $response values, and data files of up to 100 MB load without freezing the window.
  • A flow whose request script fails now takes the failure path, and background services follow a choice of no environment.
